I think it's a good idea, but there's always going to have to be at least one mod who wasn't elected. I think, better than electing mods, there should be a way for the community to vote them out of the position. If they're being unreasonably impartial, for instance, the community should have a way to remove them from power.
This is a reasonable idea. There would have to be some sort of system to prevent brigading, vote manipulation / fake votes however.

While this sounds good in practice, it wouldn't work.

If a moderator said the wrong thing once, he could be removed by users, even if he spent hours of work on a sub contributing content and moderating.

Plus, those who want to be mods will start brigading to ge themselves in positions of power, which is something I never want to happen,

I think a solution would be having an admin ran subreddit for people to voice their concerns if mods are being abusive or neglecting their position. However this would probably only work for default subs.

Speaking as a moderator of /v/politics, I would like moderators to eventually be replaced by a user-driven system of moderation. Tagging and removing inappropriate submissions could be done by group consensus instead of by moderators.

For instance, with a good coder, you could create a system wherein users tag submissions that they think should be removed. If the number of users who tag a submission for removal reaches some threshold (say, 50% as many removal tags as upgoats, and at least 50 removal tags overall) then the submission would be removed. It would then be up to the admins to decide if the post should go back up, but the initial "moderation" would be done by the community itself.

In addition to "tagging for removal," you could have similarly user-voted flair that wouldn't actually remove the article--possible flairs could be things like "False/May be misleading"; "out of date"; etc.

To minimize content manipulation by sock accounts, you could perhaps even edit the code to make it so that users can't log into a new account more than once every half hour (I'm not a coder, so I don't know how feasible that last part is, but it's something worth thinking about).

This is the system that I would eventually like to see.

At /v/politics, we are committed to transparency. That is why we've linked to the moderation log right in the sidebar.
